explanation: Keep at most k Star objects in a max heap ordered by Euclidean distance. Discard the farthest when a new star makes the heap too large. Return the retained Star objects; the judge compares their distances.
timeComplexity: O(n log(k + 1)) time. Each star makes a bounded-heap update; extracting the retained stars adds O(k log(k+1)).
spaceComplexity: O(k) auxiliary and output space. At most k+1 heap entries are live, plus k output entries.

correctness: After each insertion, removing the farthest among k+1 candidates leaves the k closest seen stars, preserving multiplicity. Induction proves the retained set is correct at the end. Equal distances permit either tied object, because the judge compares distances rather than identity.
walkthrough: The stars (2,0,0),(0,0,5),(1,2,2) have distances 2,5,3. With k=2, the third insertion removes distance 5. The callable returns the stars of distances 2 and 3; the comparator sorts by distance and checks [2,3].
edgeCases: Repeated coordinates and equal distances remain separate occurrences.
Return Star objects in this language; the wrapper compares distances and permits any output order.
